$comment: Allowed/forbidden clause combinations for the read Query DSL. Consumed by every runner (server + ts/rust/python/swift in-memory engines). Derived from the union of server/src/query/mod.rs (GET_PEERS/UNIQUE_PEERS/*_INCOMPATIBLES/*_PEERS tables), rust-client check_query_combinations + terminal executors, ts-client checkQueryCombinations + terminal executors, python-client _check_query_combinations + terminal executors, and swift-client checkQueryCombinations + terminal executors (ENH-028 phase 1, 2026-08-24/25). Two rule shapes: 'forbid' (a 2-element set that may not both be present) and 'atMostOne' (a set of which at most one member may be present — used only where every pair within the set is independently confirmed forbidden, i.e. a full clique; using atMostOne for a non-clique group would wrongly forbid two members of the group that ARE legal together, e.g. index+eq). 'message' is the server's canonical wording (server is the wire/behavior authority throughout this codebase); the corpus asserts 'code' only, per wire-corpus/README.md's determinism ruling 4 — message text is documentation, not part of the enforced contract.
